# U(1) LGT Hamiltonian and its variants



# PXP encoding
Under the approximation that adjacent sites always contains single Rydberg excitation, the original Rydberg Hamiltonian can be approximated as:
$$
\begin{align*}
&H_{\text{PXP}} = \frac{\Omega}{2}\sum_i P\,\sigma^x_i\, P + \Delta(t) \sum_i n_i, \\
&P = \prod_{\langle i,j\rangle}(1 - n_i n_j), \, n_i = \ket{r_i}\bra{r_i},
\end{align*}
$$


:::{#lem-staticSW .callout-note icon="false"}
If $\Dleta$ is constant and we take $H_0 =  \Delta(t) \sum_i n_i$ and $\varepsilon \cdot V = \frac{\Omega}{2} \cdot \sum_i P\,\sigma^x_i\, P$, the SW trasnformation gives:
$$
H_{\rm static}^{\rm SW}
=
-\Delta N
-\frac{\Omega^2}{4\Delta}
\sum_{|\Lambda|=2}
P_{\rm B}\sigma^y_{\Lambda_1}\sigma^y_{\Lambda_2}P_{\rm B}
-\frac{3}{32}\frac{\Omega^6}{\Delta^5}
\sum_{|\Lambda|=6}
P_{\rm B}
\left(
\prod_{i=1}^6\sigma^y_{\Lambda_i}
\right)
P_{\rm B}
+\cdots .
$$
:::
